note: Curated home ecosystem per playable, judged from the profile text (preferred areas, water use, seasonal habits), its real-animal analogs and its map. Each playable has one home ecosystem; `also` lists places it regularly visits. Food-chain levels are derived from diet and game tier (see `levels`); `level` on a profile overrides that with a reason.

ecosystems.label: Sea & Coast
ecosystems.description: Open ocean, reefs, beaches, sea stacks and the coastal strip where the sea shapes daily life.

ecosystems.label: Rivers, Lakes & Swamps
ecosystems.description: Rivers, lakes, bogs, mudflats and riverbanks: life organised around fresh water.

ecosystems.label: Forest
ecosystems.description: Redwoods, jungle, woodland clearings and forested hills: cover, ambush and territory.

ecosystems.label: Plains & Savanna
ecosystems.description: Open country where the big herds migrate and the hunters follow them.

ecosystems.label: Desert & Canyons
ecosystems.description: Dry canyons, scrub, oases and salt rocks: heat, scarce water and long distances.

ecosystems.label: Mountains & Cliffs
ecosystems.description: Cliffs, ledges, caves and rocky outcrops in the high hills.

levels.label: Apex predators
levels.rule: Carnivore of game tier Apex or Giant

levels.label: Small predators & scavengers
levels.rule: Carnivore of game tier Small or Tiny

levels.label: Giant grazers
levels.rule: Herbivore of game tier Apex or Giant, or a filter feeder

levels.label: Herbivores
levels.rule: Herbivore of game tier Large or Medium

levels.label: Small prey
levels.rule: Herbivore of game tier Small or Tiny: the end of the food chain

tylosaurus.reason: An orca of the open sea: pods migrate along the coast and beach-hunting families patrol the shores.

kaiwhekea.reason: Sea lion and sea turtle: swims the open sea near the surface and basks on beaches.

metriacanthosaurus.reason: The profile says it prefers coastal environments; it cools off in shallow water and courts on the mudflats.

eurhinosaurus.reason: A bottlenose dolphin: shoals circle their home waters between fish spots, rocks and underwater caves.

austroraptor.reason: Heron and emperor penguin: fishes coasts and seaways; its preferred areas are mostly coast and ocean.

tropeognathus.reason: Herring gull and cormorant: spends its whole life on the coast and at sea and nests on sea stacks.

leedsichthys.levelReason: A filter feeder: like the whale shark it eats plankton and small fish, so it sits with the giant grazers rather than the predators.
leedsichthys.reason: A whale shark on a great open-sea migration loop.

camptosaurus.reason: A quokka of coasts and island scrub; its map marks coastal, island and forest-edge areas.

spinosaurus.reason: Claims medium water sources in bogs, mudflats and jungle rivers; its territory ends 10 body lengths from the water.

deinosuchus.reason: A Nile crocodile of rivers and estuaries that also crosses the sea between islands; Spinosaurus drives it out of the same rivers.

suchomimus.reason: A gharial that drifts between lakes and rivers and nests close to a Spinosaurus.

sarcosuchus.reason: A mugger crocodile moving between swamps, ponds and forest rivers and defending mud pools in the dry season.

concavenator.reason: A giant otter: semi-aquatic along shores and marshes and nests communally on its marsh nesting ground.

thalassodromeus.reason: Flocks travel inland along rivers and lakes and nest at a big lake; they court in the mountains.

deinocheirus.reason: Mute swan and moose: spends its life by lakes and rivers, diving for lakeweed and fleeing into the water.

lurdusaurus.reason: A hippo: in the water by day, males hold water territories, mud baths against the sun.

lambeosaurus.reason: Travels along waterways and crosses them back and forth to shake off predators.

halszkaraptor.reason: A mallard of ponds, lakes and rivers that skims the water for lakeweed and small fish.

tyrannosaurus.reason: Primarily found in forests; claims the Redwoods, the southern hills and Wollemi as territory.

tyrannotitan.reason: A tiger of hills, forests and wetlands; males claim a whole POI and cool off in ponds.

ceratosaurus.reason: A grey wolf pack that strongly prefers woodland and clearings.

dilophosaurus.reason: Red fox and raccoon of woods and hills, blending in with optional chromatophores.

achillobator.reason: A nocturnal caracal roaming woods and wetland edges beside its Latenivenatrix rookery.

latenivenatrix.reason: Rook and dhole: rookeries settle in forests and wetlands with a shared nest territory.

compsognathus.reason: A rat that follows one large carnivore, most often Tyrannosaurus, through the forest.

therizinosaurus.reason: A cassowary that spends most of its life deep in the forest and patrols it at night.

eotriceratops.reason: Asian elephant and hippo: the matriarch leads the herd through forest and hill country.

stegosaurus.reason: A black rhino camping on food bushes and water in forests and hills.

iguanodon.reason: A cape buffalo roaming forests and hills and claiming food and water on the way.

anodontosaurus.reason: A sedentary wombat of hills, woods and wetland edges living on fruit, roots and nuts.

albertaceratops.reason: Badger and wild boar: roots in woodland and moves to rivers and mud pits in the dry season.

kentrosaurus.reason: Settles inside a Stegosaurus territory and stays near rivers and shaded pools.

tenontosaurus.reason: A peccary that tramples through forest territories digging for tubers.

torvosaurus.reason: An African lion pride holding open country: canyons, coasts, hills and forest edges.

hatzegopteryx.reason: A golden eagle whose mated pairs hold whole POIs over open country, canyons and coasts.

quetzalcoatlus.reason: A vulture that follows the migrating herds and predators to their dying grounds.

alioramus.reason: African wild dogs that travel long distances behind the herds.

kelenken.reason: A secretary bird of open plains and rocky ground.

deinonychus.reason: A spotted hyena that trails large herds and apex carnivores across open ground.

rhamphorhynchus.reason: An oxpecker roosting on the sauropods of the open plains.

argentinosaurus.reason: A giraffe of open country that struggles in forest.

apatosaurus.reason: An elephant migrating across open country with mud wallows as waypoints.

parasaurolophus.reason: Red deer and wild horse on long generational migration loops.

amargasaurus.reason: Wildebeest and giraffe following the sauropod migration routes.

pachyrhinosaurus.reason: Musk ox and caribou migrating long distances between feeding and nesting grounds.

styracosaurus.reason: Musk ox and oryx roaming arid grasslands in huge herds.

citipati.reason: Prefers clearings and open land where danger can be seen coming, travelling with sauropods.

struthiomimus.reason: An ostrich that loves traversing vast open lands alongside other herds.

psittacosaurus.reason: A meerkat sentry travelling with the ceratopsian herds.

giganotosaurus.reason: A nomad of canyons, coasts and forest edges; its preferred areas start at Dry Fang Canyon.

allosaurus.reason: The profile says it prefers arid environments: canyons, rock and scrub, sheltering from the midday sun.

pycnonemosaurus.reason: An endless nomad across canyons, hills and forests, driven by its appetite.

utahraptor.reason: Wolf family packs holding territories in canyons, hills and forests.

megalania.reason: A Komodo dragon; the arid variant basks in Dry Fang Canyon and Sharptooth Oasis (the temperate variant lives in bogs).

barsboldia.reason: A Bactrian camel: arid-dwelling, travels to Salt Rocks and goes long without water.

yunnanosaurus.reason: Moose and red kangaroo: prefers arid ground in the rainy season and returns to water in the dry season.

yutyrannus.reason: A snow leopard of cool hills and forests that defends resting and nesting dens.

daspletosaurus.reason: A cougar that primarily travels through forests and cliffsides.

maip.reason: A hyena that loses pursuers in rocky outcrops and complicated terrain.

pachycephalosaurus.reason: A mountain goat that thrives in mountains and settles around a chosen rock, cliff or cave.

dryosaurus.reason: Rabbit and baboon: claims caves and perches in the hills and flees into small caves.
